paragraphs: The wife of Rabbi Eliezer ben Hyrkanos. She was the daughter of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who was executed, and the sister of Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh. She is mentioned in Shabbat 116a, which relates that she and her brother Rabban Gamliel showed the falsehoods of a gentile judge who took bribes. In Nedarim 20b they asked her why her sons were exceedingly beautiful, and she answered how her husband Rabbi Eliezer conducted himself with her with the utmost modesty. In Bava Metzia 59b: in the dispute over the oven of Akhnai, in which Rabbi Eliezer and the sages disagreed and they set him apart from them, from that day on she did not let Rabbi Eliezer fall on his face [in prayer]. Once, on Rosh Chodesh — she thought it was Rosh Chodesh, but in fact it was the eve of Rosh Chodesh — she was not careful to watch him, and found him fallen on his face. Then she said to him: “Get up, for you have killed my brother.” He asked: “How do you know?” She said to him: “So I have received from my father’s father’s house: all the gates are locked except the gate of wronging.”

notes.text: The compressed Rosh Chodesh/eve sequence follows Hyman. Abbreviated Eliezer is connected to the full Eliezer ben Hyrkanos heading, and Gamliel is the named brother, without global abbreviation expansion.

Bava Metzia 59b includes the full/deficient-month confusion and an alternate poor-person interruption before the prayer and death report. Hyman’s compressed Rosh Chodesh wording is retained rather than silently harmonized to one consulted account.
